key_insight: The paper shows that bridging homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization is fundamentally hard: common similarity assumptions are not enough to beat pessimistic time bounds, and only a stronger combination of assumptions yields a better result.
engineering_relevance: For distributed training systems, this means you should not expect asynchronous speedups from weak data-similarity assumptions alone; achieving tighter wall-clock guarantees may require stronger structural conditions on local objectives.
method: Proves impossibility results for any randomized algorithm under standard first- and second-order similarity assumptions.
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone still cannot close the gap.
Introduces strong interpolation plus local Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions to derive an improved time complexity bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and complexity bounds, comparing homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization under different assumption sets.
watch_item: The improved guarantee depends on strong structural assumptions that may be difficult to verify or satisfy in real-world distributed learning setups.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
